speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin, Miss Cheng Li Hui and Mr Ang Wei Neng have asked about the status of the Kuala Lumpur-Singapore High Speed Rail Project (HSR).

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Many Singaporeans are asking the same question following numerous statements by Malaysian leaders on the HSR Project over the past two months.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: These statements suggest that Malaysia no longer intends to continue with the Project in accordance with what both countries agreed under the HSR Bilateral Agreement (BA).

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Dr Mahathir was also quoted as saying that "It's   not beneficial.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: It's going to cost us a huge sum of money, we will make no money at all from this operation".

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: He also said that Malaysia may have to pay "almost 500 million" as a "penalty" although he was unsure of the currency.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: On 1 June, Dr Mahathir reiterated that the decision to cancel the HSR Project was done by the Pakatan Harapan government, because from "the very beginning, we campaigned on that issue and we won't go away from the decision of the party".

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: On 3 June, Johor Menteri Besar, Dato' Osman Sapian, was quoted in the Malaysian media as saying that "short-term losses of RM500 million" from terminating the HSR Project were better than for the Malaysian government to "bear the debt burden of more than RM100 billion" if it continues the HSR Project.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: On 11 June, in an interview with the Nikkei Asian Review in Tokyo, Dr Mahathir then said that the HSR Project was "postponed".

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Malaysian Transport Minister Mr Anthony Loke and Finance Minister Mr Lim Guan Eng later told the press on separate occasions that they, together with Economic Affairs Minister Dato' Seri Mohd Azmin bin Ali, would visit Singapore to discuss the HSR Project.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Various other reports then appeared in the Malaysian media citing an "alternative" proposal to the Malaysian Council of Eminent Persons to utilise the existing double-track of Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) to run trains at 200 kilometres per hour (km/h), which would take 130 minutes to travel from Kuala Lumpur to Singapore.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: According to these media reports, the 'alternative' plan would purportedly mean that Malaysia would "not need to renegotiate with Singapore".

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Malaysian social media also carried articles stating that Singapore has a "moral responsibility" not to "bully" Malaysia, and to cancel the HSR Project with minimum penalty.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: After several years of discussion, Singapore and Malaysia signed the HSR BA in December 2016.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: This BA is an international treaty that is binding on the countries that signed it.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: In other words, both Singapore and Malaysia are legally bound to perform our obligations under the BA, regardless of any changes in the government.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The HSR Project agreed under the BA is a high-speed rail that would allow travellers to commute from Jurong Lake District in Singapore to the Bandar Malaysia development in Kuala Lumpur in 90 minutes.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The key success factor of this Project is the 90-minute travel time that provides greater convenience for travellers.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Ninety minutes is significantly less than the travel time by road or by the existing railway and is competitive with the 50-minute flight time between Changi Airport and Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), plus airport transfers.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: To achieve the 90-minute travel time, trains operating the HSR's international Express Service between Singapore and Kuala Lumpur have to run at speeds of 300 km/h or more on a dual track line designed for a top speed of 350 km/h.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: This requirement is essential, as otherwise it would make less sense for a traveller to make a day trip from Singapore to Kuala Lumpur, or vice versa, using the HSR rather than by air.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: After signing the BA, Singapore acquired land to facilitate the construction of HSR, passed legislation in Parliament, and set up an Infrastructure Company, SG HSR Pte Ltd under the Land Transport Authority.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We have formed a team of more than 100 specialists in the company to build, own, fund and maintain the HSR civil infrastructure in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: These staff have worked hard to fulfill our obligations to meet a challenging implementation timeline.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The tenders for the HSR civil infrastructure in Singapore, as well as the joint tender with Malaysia to appoint an Assets Company (AssetsCo) are underway.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: By May this year, SG HSR had called five tenders to construct the HSR civil infrastructure within Singapore.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We have also started engaging potential bidders for the remaining major tenders.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: All these works cost money, including costs for consultancies to design the civil infrastructure, costs for dedicating manpower to oversee and deliver the Project, and costs for land acquisition.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: This is actual money that has already been spent, our taxpayers' money.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We can recover value for some of the expenditure, even if the HSR Project does not proceed.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But the significant amount which has been spent will be completely wasted expenditure, if the project does not proceed.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: To date, Singapore has still not received a reply from the Malaysian government.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The public statements made by the Malaysian Ministers and Prime Minister Dr Mahathir himself on the termination of the Project have not been followed through with any official communication to us.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: At this point, therefore, we have been left with no choice but to continue performing in accordance with the BA and thus continue to incur more costs.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: For the month of July, this month, we expect to also incur more than S$6 million.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: These include our ongoing manpower costs, operating expenses and contract costs.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: It will be most unfortunate if Malaysia has, in fact, decided to terminate but delays in notifying us, because there will be further wasted expenditure.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The HSR BA is a fair treaty, with equal rights and obligations on both sides.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: It is worth noting again that it was Malaysia which had suggested the HSR and Singapore agreed to the joint project.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: If the HSR Project is terminated because of the actions of country A, then country A should compensate country B for expenses that have already been incurred by country B, in accordance with the BA.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: It would not be fair for the taxpayers of one country to bear the cost of another country’s actions.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The Singapore Government has a duty to all Singaporeans to be accountable for the substantial public funds spent on the HSR Project.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Because the costs that we have incurred will add to the total amount of compensation, it is in Malaysia’s own interest to officially inform us of its position on the HSR Project early, to minimise the amounts involved.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I highlighted this consideration to Economic Affairs Minister Dato’ Seri Mohd Azmin bin Ali when he called me on 6 June 2018.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Dato’ Seri Azmin Ali suggested that both countries’ officials meet to discuss the HSR Project.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I asked him for details on the scope of the discussion so that the meeting could be productive.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: He agreed and promised to send me a letter on the details.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Our High Commissioner in Kuala Lumpur has also conveyed the same points to Malaysian Transport Minister Mr Anthony Loke and Finance Minister Mr Lim Guan Eng.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: However, we have yet to receive the details from Malaysia.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Besides costs incurred by Singapore, rail consortia from China, Japan, Europe and other interested parties, such as international financial institutions, have also been incurring costs preparing their bids for the HSR AssetsCo tender, which was jointly launched by Singapore and Malaysia last December.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: These companies have taken the HSR Project very seriously, including working with their governments to seek clarification on the requirements of the HSR AssetsCo tender over the past seven months.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Following the recent statements by Malaysian leaders, the bidders have sought urgent clarification from Singapore and Malaysia on the status of the HSR Project.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: It is not tenable for them to proceed with their bids without knowing if the project is off, or to put their consortia and resources on hold indefinitely with the attendant opportunity and financing costs.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The Singapore Government will continue to press for official clarification from the Malaysian government.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: There are appropriate processes at law in case Malaysia should wish to propose changes to the BA, or to terminate it.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: If the Malaysian Government fails to provide an official response, then we cannot ignore the public statements made by the Malaysian Ministers, and Prime Minister Dr Mahathir himself, on the termination of the Project, and Singapore will act according to its rights.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Every day, several hundred thousand commuter trips are made between Singapore and Malaysia through our land checkpoints.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: When completed, the RTS Link will ease congestion significantly at our land checkpoints and make it much more convenient for people to travel between Singapore and JB.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: On 30 May, Malaysian Transport Minister Mr Anthony Loke told Channel NewsAsia that “the RTS will proceed”, although Malaysia would “have to re-study the project in terms of cost and so on”.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The following day, he also told our Shin Min newspaper that he hoped the project could be accelerated.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: However, we have not heard anything officially from the Malaysians on their intentions on the RTS Link.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: To proceed or, indeed, speed up the project, many implementation issues have to be sorted out.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: As with HSR, we also have an RTS Link BA with the Malaysians.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Under the terms of that agreement, Singapore’s Singapore Mass Rapid Transit (SMRT) and Malaysia’s Prasarana Malaysia Berhad needed to incorporate a Joint-Venture Company to become the RTS Link operator by 30 June this year.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: That did not happen, as Prasarana had suspended discussions with SMRT after Malaysia’s General Elections.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: This means that both countries should now proceed to call an open, international tender to appoint the RTS Link operator, unless we mutually agree on a postponement of the deadline.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: In the meantime, we will continue to work with Malaysia to reduce congestion through other means.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But it has to be based on the cardinal principle of respecting the sanctity of international law and international agreements.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: For Singapore, we also need to safeguard Singapore’s hard-earned reputation as a credible and consistent partner, and a country that abides fully by our international obligations.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Both Malaysia and Singapore urgently need to answer the questions from interested bidders for the HSR AssetsCo tender, and we await Malaysia’s clarification so that, as responsible partners who have called the tender, we can do so.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: It is, therefore, in Malaysia’s own interest to clarify its position early.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: First is just to clarify one more time, under the agreement, there is no penalty for terminating the contract except for compensation.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: My second question is: what is the budgetary figure for the HSR for the Singapore portion?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: The last question is: if things do not go well, what is the recourse for Singapore?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Is it an international court or is it a court of Singapore or Malaysia to resolve the issue of termination, if there is?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: All these are terms which are covered within the BA.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I cannot speak in much detail because I am also bound by the confidentiality clause within the BA.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: So, these are, as I said, all taxpayers' money.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: And we, as a Government, have to be accountable to our people.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: It depends on actual tender bids in due course when we receive and award them.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: It is not our practice to disclose those sums so as not to bias the tenders.
